4. The learned Advocate for the petitioner contends that the Ordinance being published in the Bangladesh Gazette on April 29, 1976, came into force on that date and hence in view of Section 9 of the General Clauses Act, that date should be excluded in computing the period of limitation prescribed under section 4(1) of the Ordinance, and if that is done, the application for restoration of the land was within time. The learned Advocate for the opposite party No.2, on the other hand, argues that the period of six months provided under Section 4(1) of the Ordinance is inclusive of the day on which the Ordinance was published in the Bangladesh Gazette and as such 29th April, 1976, should be counted in computing the period of limitation. Consequently the last date for filing the application for restoration of the land transferred during the period, of economic distress will be 28th October, 1976, and since the application was filed on 29th October, 1976, the application was out of time by one day. 

 5. Section 4(1) of the Ordinance, inter alia, provides that an application for restoration of agricultural land transferred the period of economic distress is to be filed within 6 months "from the commencement of this Ordinance." Since however, the Ordinance is silent as to the date of its coming into force. The term `commencement' used in the section must mean the day on which the Ordinance was published in the Bangladesh Gazette, i.e. 29 April, 1976. Both parties are agreed on this. But their controversy is over the question whether the date of publication of the Ordinance should be counted in calculating the period of limitation prescribed in the section. The expression from preceding the words the commencement of this Ordinance" occurring in Section 4(1) is a clear indicative of the method to be adopted for the purpose of computation of the prescribed period of limitation Section 9 read with section 30 of the General Clauses Act, inter alia, says that in any Act or Ordinance it shall be sufficient, for the :purpose of excluding the first in a series of days or any other period of time, to use the word "from", which means that if the word: "from" is used instance, the first day is to be excluded. Acting on this principle, I have, therefore, no hesitation to hold that the application for restoration of the land was clearly within time and the learned Munsif (now Assistant Judge) committed an error of law in holding the same to be barred by limitation.
